sentences.text: The genus Riparovenator contains only one known species, Riparovenator milnerae, which is estimated to be 10.6 meters long, up to 2.65 meters tall at the hip, and weigh between 4.3 and 4.8 tonnes.
The genus name Riparovenator means 'riverbank hunter' in Latin.
Riparovenator is considered the second largest carnivorous theropod dinosaur in Europe, after Megalosaurus bucklandii.

The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes premaxillary bodies, a disarticulated braincase, and a partial lacrimal and prefrontal bone, while referred remains include a posterior nasal fragment and a series of twenty-two tail vertebrae, totaling around fifty bones.

Spinosaurid fossils were uncovered between 2013 and 2017 at a beach near Chilton Chine in Britain, and all known fossil material of Riparovenator was recovered from the Wessex Formation at Chilton Chine.
Fossils now identified as Riparovenator were historically misidentified as belonging to the genus Baryonyx.

The species Riparovenator milnerae was formally named and described in 2021 by a team including Chris T. Barker, David W. E. Hone, and Darren Naish, and the specific name milnerae honors Angela Milner, who died in August 2021.
Riparovenator likely fed on aquatic prey like fish and turtles, as well as terrestrial prey including young crocodiles, baby dinosaurs, and mammals.
Researchers suggest that high diversity among spinosaurids in the same area may have been caused by environmental conditions that benefited their ecological niche.
Riparovenator belongs to the family Spinosauridae, is classified within the subfamily Baryonychinae, and is placed in the tribe Ceratosuchopsini.

Barker et al. (2021) classified Ceratosuchops as the sister taxon to Riparovenator within the subfamily Baryonychinae, and Riparovenator is recovered as a member of the clade Ceratosuchopsini, closely related to Ceratosuchops and Suchomimus, with Ceratosuchops as its sister taxon.
In 2022, Sereno and colleagues tentatively proposed combining Ceratosuchops and Riparovenator into a single taxonomic unit.

Riparovenator lived during the Early Cretaceous (Barremian) period in what is now Britain, and Riparovenator lived approximately between 129 and 125 million years ago during the Barremian stage in Europe.
The time range for Riparovenator is estimated from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
It is debated whether similar and closely related spinosaurids could coexist by overlapping in ecological requirements rather than partitioning resources.
